name: provider_null_incoming_calls surfaced via 'dependency injection'/'Depends()' wording, marker and hedge in separate sentences
description: task-m2-python-preset.md stage 6 addendum 3, revised: the marker ('dependency injection'/'Depends()') and the 'this is not evidence that no caller exists' hedge are deliberately in DIFFERENT sentences, not one - this is the shape cli-contract.md's/SKILL.md's own 'Fixed summary shape' actually recommends (evidence boundary and limitation disclosure as separate sentences), so it is the representative case, not the same-sentence phrasing this fixture originally used. An earlier fix (widening the exclusion anchor to all four LIMITATION_SURFACE_PATTERNS.provider_null_incoming_calls phrases, still requiring the marker to be nearby) covered the same-sentence shape but not this one, because its [^.!?]* span cannot cross a sentence boundary to find the marker - reviewer measurement (task-m2-python-preset.md stage 6 addendum 3) found this exact separate-sentence summary still wrongly flagged stale_index_caveat under indexingStatus: ready. The real fix drops the marker requirement entirely: 'not evidence/proof ... no caller(s) exist(s)' is, by its own grammar, always a claim about caller existence, so it is excluded unconditionally, in whatever sentence it appears (see CALLER_EXISTENCE_UNCERTAINTY_PHRASE). Non-vacuity: reconstructing the marker-anchored fix (the version this fixture originally locked in) and running it against this exact summary confirms it would still wrongly flag stale_index_caveat. Must-pass fixture 14.
